extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, technologists, journalists, and the general public interested in tech policy, disinformation, and public-comment systems
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis of a large-scale fake-comment campaign targeting FCC net-neutrality proceedings, with policy and technical recommendations to detect, deter, and respond to automated/impersonation-driven disinformation in public comment systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit submission of false or unauthorized comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress and state governments should prohibit the submission of false comments or comments on behalf of an individual that are not expressly authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a legislative fix proposed by the New York Attorney General to make submission of fake comments explicitly illegal; intended to create a statutory basis to penalize actors who flood public comment systems with fabricated or unauthorised submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend impersonation laws to impose substantial penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend impersonation laws to provide for substantial penalties when many individuals are impersonated before a government agency or official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal targets large-scale impersonation campaigns (mass impersonation) used to influence government decision-making; legislative change would enable harsher punishment for actors who impersonate many people in the context of public-comment campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require technical safeguards for public comment intake (e.g., CAPTCHAs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Governments and other entities accepting public comments should have technical safeguards, such as CAPTCHA systems, to combat automated comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offered as a straightforward mitigation but explicitly caveated: AI systems have been shown to defeat some CAPTCHA systems, so CAPTCHAs are necessary but not sufficient; technical safeguards should be part of a layered defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design public comment systems to account for manipulative activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Public comment systems should be designed in the future to take manipulative activities into account when gauging public interest and input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design principle emphasizing systemic changes (not just detection): incorporate mechanisms to detect manipulation, consider provenance and authenticity, and build processes that reduce the ability of mass-fabricated comments to skew apparent public opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance privacy/anonymity with verification of commenter existence
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be a tension between respect for privacy and anonymity, and a need to gauge whether the people speaking actually exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policymakers and designers must trade off protecting anonymous speech and ensuring comments represent real, distinct people; solutions should consider privacy-preserving verification or other approaches that limit abuse while respecting civil liberties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop detection tools beyond basic forensic algorithms
rubrics_metrics.description: Contending with this threat will have to go beyond basic forensic algorithms and will have to contend with a fundamental aspect of today's internet where anonymity has both advantages and disadvantages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning that simple forensic methods are insufficient against rapidly improving synthetic-text and impersonation capabilities; calls for more advanced, holistic tools and approaches that account for system-level anonymity and adversarial adaptation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat AI-generated synthetic text as a large-scale threat
rubrics_metrics.description: New technologies to automatically generate text, such as GPT-3 (and earlier GPT-2), can be used to automatically generate plausible text at scale; volunteers in a study could not distinguish synthetic posts from real ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that synthetic-text generation enables plausible, large-volume comment campaigns; detection, policy, and system design must assume high-quality automated text will be used to manipulate public processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and restrict deceptive lead-generation and co-registration tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead generation campaigns used co-registration sites to collect personal information, promising 'free cash,' gift cards, product samples, and other lures — tactics that co-opt vulnerable individuals' identities and fabricate responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigations could include regulating or monitoring lead-generation practices, requiring transparency about data collection and reuse, and prohibiting deceptive inducements that result in misused identities in public-comment submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and address 'Impersonation-as-a-Service' criminal infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Criminal services exist that collect user credentials via malware and match this capability with marketplaces to deliver 'complete user profiles to attackers' (Impersonation-as-a-Service).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Threat model: impersonation marketplaces enable mass, high-fidelity identity theft for use in comment campaigns; responses should include cybersecurity enforcement, takedowns, and cross-sector information-sharing to disrupt these platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit reliance on public comments to justify regulatory decisions when manipulated
rubrics_metrics.description: Americans' voices are being drowned out by fake comments; agencies should not use manipulated public comments as a means to justify votes or decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulators should validate the integrity of comment datasets before citing them as evidence of public support; where manipulation is suspected, agencies should refrain from relying on raw comment counts to justify outcomes and should disclose investigations and findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use enforcement actions and transparency (investigations, settlements, reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigation by the New York Attorney General resulted in settlements with lead generation companies and public disclosure of findings (e.g., 8.5 million fake comments, impersonated individuals' quotes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforcement — investigations, civil settlements, public reporting — is a mechanism to deter and remediate abuse; transparency about methods and victims (e.g., publishing examples of impersonation) raises awareness and supports policy change.
